description: goal: see how long the pumpkin cheesecake would last among 3 girls, and see who would end up having the last bite
who_was_playing: Three of my friends who are also my roommates (ages 20). Player 1 and 2 suggested to share the remainder of a cheesecake we had in the fridge, then Person 1 abruptly suggested the example of play stated previously.
trust_why: This interaction only happened because we are all friends and comfortable in each other’s presence, which led to sharing cheesecake. Being familiar and lighthearted with each other led into an organic playful encounter with one another. I feel that the people I’m with play greatly in the role of an establishment of trust and safety for play to occur.
playful_why: The object was food, which was the contribution to this example of play.
pull_why: We were curious to see who would get to have the last bite
signs_why: At first we were all taking random spoonfuls, after the suggestion of the play, each spoonful was planned and ordered, Person A took a bite, then Person B, then Person C.
feeling_why: I can see both joy and silliness included in this activity since it was friendly competition by playing with food
anything_else: Play is not very common among my age group, unless it’s planned, like a board game, card game, video game, etc. This example is spontaneous and not a traditional definition of play, almost childish as it encourages imagination and curiosity.

description: Friend plays video game blind while other friends watch, chat, and voice the characters
who_was_playing:
Player 1 - played the game for the first time, voice acted narration
Players 2-4 - mega-fans of the game, watched and cheered Player 1 on, whispered about spoilers/theories amongst ourselves, voice acted characters, light backseat gaming/hint giving
trust_why: We were very silly, voice acting boistrously, and Player 1 was the only one who had never played the game before, so there was a level of vulnerability we all agreed to, because we were amongst friends who wouldn't reject each other for it.
playful_why: Player 1 has big hands, and the original laptop keyboard had small keys that made playing the game frustrating and difficult. When we switched it out to a big bluetooth keyboard, they not only could play the game better (and have more fun)- they could ease onto the floor and get comfy as they pleased.
pull_why: The video game we played has a lot of challenges, and Player 1 had most fun trying to figure out the puzzling aspects of it. Meanwhile, Players 2-4 had fun coming up with unique, boisterous voices for each wacky character.
signs_why: Our voices were loud, sometimes yelling (we quieted down to be kind to the neighbors) as we voiced the characters and cheered on Player 1. Other times our voices were quieter, as we whispered to each other about spoilers, or Player 1 was narrating less important dialogue. We would gasp and laugh at our favorite parts of the game, or when Player 1 would surprise/impress us with their gameplay.
anything_else: We were also eating homemade brownies :) very important detail

description: The two people I watched on the seesaw mainly talked while swinging/seesawing, smiling a little bit but mainly appearing calm and content chatting with each other. There was a point where one of the two pressed his weight into the ground to keep the other suspended in the air. The seesaw was mainly an activity in the background of their conversation, and I chatted with them a bit after walking over to take their picture.
who_was_playing: Player 1 and 2: Both freshman engineering major boys.
trust_why: Since using a seesaw requires two people, I think the biggest contributor in this case is the people. Both of boys were already walking, saw the seesaw, and in a moment of spontaneity, decided to continue their conversation there. If either had passed the seesaw while walking by themselves, they wouldn't have used it. Therefore, i think the people was the biggest factor in allowing the play to happen.
playful_why: The motion of the seesaw is interactive and playful, with the two "players" working together to boost each other into the air. That movement is the play that the seesaw provides.
pull_why: I think what pulled them in was purely the whim of "Why not?" There isn't an urgency to using a seesaw, but there is curiousity there, and indulging in an activity that they may not have had the chance to in a while. Having the seesaw on campus is an invitation, so why not?
signs_why: While I did see them smiling while talking, the most obvious indicator of play was them actually playing on the seesaw and pushing each other into the air. It wasn't exxagerated, but they were engaging with the object, having fun being propelled in the air or keeping the other suspended in the air.
feeling_why: I think that using a seesaw could result in a number of the options above, but specifically the two people I observed seemed to just be more happy and content while on the seesaw. They were calm but clearly enjoying themselves, given their relaxed demeanor and smiles, and their general excitement when I asked to take a picture of them for this form.

description: A trick on a bike where the user pedals forward and backward with the front wheel rotated to balance the bike upright and stationary.
who_was_playing: There was really only one player: the boy on his bike, but he had 2-3 friends nearby observing.
trust_why: I see time as the most important factor, because something like this takes considerable practice. For it to feel safe, he needed to have spent that time getting comfortable with the trick.
playful_why: It might be more appropriate to say that it was playful due to the lack of motion. An upright and balanced bike is expected to be in motion, so the playfulness comes from the diversion of that.
pull_why: I think "challenge" might be a more obvious answer initially, but I think the boy probably engaged in the activity more so for the attention or respect that it would draw to him. He was most likely already confident in his ability to perform it, so I don't think he was truly wondering to himself "can I?"
signs_why: The visible act of performing the trick on the bike through his posture and movement showed a clear effort and intent to perform something unconventional with no clear or tangible motive, which implied play.
feeling_why: While he most was hoping to instill awe or wonder in others, I think his feeling while engaging in the activity primarily would be of deep focus, as it required constant bodily adjustments to maintain a steady balance.

description: At 11 PM on Saturday, my friends and I decided to play the ID game. | How to Play Everyone puts their IDs on the table One person is selected to pick a question out of any of the rounds, and is tasked with ordering the IDs from most to least likely They reveal the round of questions they selected from, and the group is tasked with guessing which question that person chose. After they guess, the orderer explains why they ordered it the way they did, allowing for funny memories.
who_was_playing:
10 of my closest friends at school. We all met freshman year and have made many memories along our college careers that shape our perceptions of one another. 

There was a player 1 who was chosen at random. This person is the ID orderer

The other players served as multiple Player 2s, they were in charge of guessing the question that the orderer ranked the IDs by.
medium: Digital - the rules were loaded on all of our phones. Analog - Used physical IDs
trust_why: We were comfortable sharing our opinions of others with them because we have been friends for a long time and did not feel like we were offending them in any way.
playful_why: The shape of the IDs was helpful because it allowed us to properly distinguish each other when making the order. It became playful when someone decided to use a non-ID that allowed their true identity to still be distinguishable.
pull_why: Time was a constraint since we started so late, creating urgency to play sooner and gather everyone together. The urgency did not allow for many questions to be asked while playing, which allowed the game to flow smoother.
signs_why: Everyone was constantly smiling while playing because they were enjoying the moment of the game. The face also served a purpose to the game as an important skill to have as the orderer was to remain stoic until everyone made their guesses, while the other players were smiling while trying to read the orderer’s face.
feeling_why: Instead of trying to play the game to win as the orderer, we all started picking questions that were the funniest to make everyone laugh once they figured it out and the orderer explained their choices.
anything_else: The game perfectly represented the aspect of play because of how spontaneous yet fulfilng the experience was. The most important emotion that was felt was unity. Despite spending all day with each other and having a long dinner where memories were already shared, we decided to keep making more by playing a new game. Not only did we all leave the experience laughing and smiling, but we learned something new about everyone and found a new way to strengthen our bond: the ID game.

description: At dinner, my friend and I got isolated into a separate conversation. She noticed a logo on my shirt and thought it looked like another logo. I was quite rattled she did not know the logo, and out of sympathy I asked her to show me a logo I would not know. Eventually, we kept going back and forth and the rest of the table joined in on our game.
who_was_playing:
Player 1, my friend who started the game by asking me the question

Player 2, myself who decided to ask a follow-up question that led to a mini game between us
trust_why: I felt comfortable pointing out how funny it was she did not know the initial logo. Since she felt comfortable with the joke I made, we were able to make a game out of a situation that normally could end in someone taking offense to the initial remark.
key_tool: Logos on the google images we searched on our phones
playful_why: The colors of the logo helped the players imagine where they have seen it before. It became playful once we started finding logos that were obscure and not easy to guess.
pull_why: Since I was curious to my friend if she knew any logos that I did not know, we began testing out for fun which logos we were and were not aware of. I learned that she is more well-versed with coffee brands and I was more knowledgeable with sport logos.
signs: Behavior (linger, come back, repeat, invite a friend)
signs_why: We would take turns looking up a logo on our phones and hiding the name of it while showing the other person, forcing them to guess based off the image. It took time finding what logos didnt have text in it, what logos were more known than others, and thinking of what logos they might not know to come up with during this process.
feeling_why: We both enjoyed learning new logos while understanding more about each other. Instead of taking a comment to heart, we both gained immense joy while patiently waiting for our food to arrive.
anything_else: If you are ever bored and need a game to play, whip out your phone and make a bet with your friend(s) to see if they can guess the logo!

activity: Adding random shelves to my room
description: I woke up on Sunday, found out my new shelves were delivered early, and decided to instantly start hammering them in at 11am
who_was_playing: Player 1 - myself, I just woke up and went on my phone. I saw the notification that my shelves I ordered from Amazon came early and decided to open them up.
trust_why: I had a lot of space to work with, but not a lot of tools. Thankfully the amount of space allowed me to get creative in how I leveraged myself in the best positions to hammer in the shelves and not fall.
playful_why: The hammer was initially chosen over the drill because it made a slightly quieter noise that wouldnt wake up my roommates. The sound became playful once I started making beats with the hit patterns I made.
pull_why: The emotion that I first had when seeing the shelves at my door were exciting. That excitement turned into a motivation because I knew how joyful I would be once I installed the shelves into the wall and decorated it.
signs: Behavior (linger, come back, repeat, invite a friend)
signs_why: When I decided to install the shelves, I needed to think of how to arange them. It took careful steps with placeholding the shelves, getting the bubble level to measure the straightnees before hammering away. Once I assembled the shelves, I began layfully decorating them with items that originally took up unnecessary nightstand space and envisioning what items to place and how to place them.
feeling_why: The initial feeling of calmness occurred during the play, as I decided to take a deep breath when a shelf would fall after I hammered it in rather than getting mad. I achieved a state of contentness once I took that final step back to enjoy the finished product. I realized what a good deed I did for myself while allowing visitors to be impressed when they step into my room.
anything_else: I learned in this task that remaining calm is an interesting way to play with your own emotions. I unintentionally tested how calm I could be when something did not go my way, and I did so by taking extra time to complete the task and play around with different methodologies instead of giving up. If I could apply that in other homework problems or even work related issues, I can become much more patient and achieve the successful outcome more often than not.

description: I saw students sifting through second-hand items until something caught their eyes. If a item did catch their attention they would pulled it off the rack and hold on to it and continue looking again. It was almost if they were trying to find treasure.
who_was_playing: They were multiple players about 10 at any given moment, but they can all be group in two. The buyers, the people looking for treasure and will purchase something, and the browser, the people with just looking and holding on stuff but don't end up purchasing anything.
trust_why: School create a sense of safety especially in the university setting because action here have a much higher consequence. So people are more likely to monitor their behavior.
pull_why: What if they find a piece of clothing or items that they like, I think that what pull people in.
signs: Behavior (linger, come back, repeat, invite a friend)
signs_why: Players through rack until they found something they like want or is of higher value and then repeat the process again.
feeling_why: The excitement of finding something amazing or valuable.

description: My friend was driving and my other friend decided to sit up and stick her upper body out of the window and feel the wind.
who_was_playing: Player 1: car driver, Player 2: friend sticking head out of window
trust_why: Because it was so late at night, my friend felt comfortable sticking her upper body out of the window.
playful_why: The motion of the car driving forward allowed for my friend to enjoy the wind while sticking her body out
pull_why: My friend wanted to feel the wind and adrenaline of sticking her body out of a moving car, something that would instantly satisfy her
signs_why: My friend's body outside of the window was a shocking movement but also showed her excitement and enjoyment
feeling_why: My friend was incredibly joyous as she felt the wind hit her body.

description: My friend hid behind a wall in hopes of jumping out and scaring me. She failed to scare me.
who_was_playing: Player 1: my friend who attempted to scare me
trust_why: My friend felt close enough to me in order to feel comfortable scaring me.
playful_why: The shape of the wall allowed my friend to fit behind it completely, giving her the confidence to scare me.
pull_why: My friend knew I was coming, which gave her the challenge of scaring me.
signs: Behavior (linger, come back, repeat, invite a friend)
signs_why: My friend stood in place, getting ready to jump out at me.
feeling_why: My friend thought it would be humorous to scare me and seek out a reaction.
anything_else: A good example of playing for humor and entertainment

description: Eboard members and I of the club wrestling team met up for a group dinner. We cooked, conversed, cleaned the dishes, and planned the wrestling season together.
who_was_playing: 7 people. All wrestling teammates and members of the eboard for the NEU club team.
trust_why: We've all been teammates for a minimum of 1 year, and none of us had a formal time to catchup since last year.
playful_why: Many of us were helping to cook dinner, or bringing ingredients. It was fun to see and eat the finished product
pull_why: The environment of everyone contributing pushed others to help out.
signs_why: Everyone was having a good time cooking, eating food, making jokes, etc.
feeling_why: Joy of catching up with everyone and eating good food

description: Friends and I were building a physical fantasy draft board for our league. The process was a little tedious, so we turned the building into a race to pass time and make a game out of it
who_was_playing: Myself, Friend 1, Friend 2.
trust_why: These people have been good friends of mine since the beginning of freshman year
key_tool: Pieces of paper and velcro adhesives
playful: They were components for the spontaneous game
playful_why: The draft board required velcro adhesives so every drafted player could physically get placed/stuck onto the board. This task of putting velcro on the board/paper slips turned into a race.
pull_why: The play started as a challenge to help pass time and be more efficient
signs_why: During the play, everyone was moving faster than usual
feeling_why: Everyone was focused to win the race and finish their task

description: The activity the player engages in is juggling and practicing juggling tricks in a public campus space often while students walk by or stop to watch.
who_was_playing: Player 1 (the juggler) was doing the activity and he was the only one engaging in it.
trust_why: I would say space because the environment allows him to juggle safely and freely for his play.
key_tool: The juggling balls he was using would be the most important as it what he needs to engage in the activity at all.
playful_why: he playfulness comes mainly from the continuous movement of throwing, catching, and controlling the juggling objects in different patterns and tricks
pull_why: I believe juggling involves continuously testing coordination/control and timing so Player 1 is pushed by the challenge of successfully completing tricks and improving their skill (overall just honing his craft).
signs_why: juggling requires large arm movements, hand-eye coordination, and physical adjustment as Player 1 throws and catches the objects
feeling_why: Seeing how concentrated Player 1 was in his craft despite the bustling students walking around him, it seemed like he was grounded and focused.

description: Playing a music game on an iPad that involves pressing the corresponding keys in rhythm with the music.
who_was_playing: Player 1: A college student playing a rhythm game alone.
trust_why: Quiet and comfortable space reduced distractions and helped the player focus on the rhythm game
playful_why: Music and sound cues guide the player’s timing and make the rhythm game engaging
pull_why: The player was motivated by the challenge of keeping up with the rhythm and getting a higher score
signs: Behavior (linger, come back, repeat, invite a friend)
signs_why: The player repeatedly tapped to the rhythm and continued playing through the song
feeling_why: The player seemed fully focused on the rhythm and timing of the game

description: Each of us took turns lifting a card above our heads (1-10), and the others say, "They're a 10 but...". Based on the severity of the red flag, the player must guess what the true number is.
who_was_playing:
Player 1 - has card (1-10) above head
Players 2-4 - can see card and are coming up with red flags to give Player 1 a hint as to what the number is, based on common sense / personal preferences
trust_why: The people are what make the game fun- each round is personalized to the Player 1's preferences, and Player 2-4's wit/understanding.
playful_why: The cards were bright and colorful.
pull_why: The game is personalized to the Player 1
signs_why: Laughter, raised voices

description: A group of students were engaging in acting exercises and going around in a circle tying different exercises.
who_was_playing: Around 6 players, Player 1 who was coming up with the prompts and Player 2-6 acting them out (Player 1 was also acting)
trust_why: The group created a sense of trust by participating together and responding openly to each person’s prompt. Since everyone was willing to act and be expressive and potentially look silly. It made the space feel supportive and comfortable enough for everyone to fully participate.
key_tool: The verbal prompts and the circle formation
playful_why: The activity depended on physical movement and acting out each prompt. The players used gestures, facial expressions, and body movement to respond creatively which made the exercise feel playful and expressive.
pull_why: Each new acting prompt created an unknown situation so the players had to see what would happen and respond in the moment. The lack of predictability of each exercise kept the activity interesting and encouraged everyone to keep participating.
signs_why: The players used exaggerated gestures and movement while acting out the prompts. Their physical commitment to the exercises made the play visible and showed that they were fully participating in the activity.
feeling_why: The acting exercises encouraged the players to be creative, exaggerated, spontaneous, and even silly. The unusual prompts and everyone’s reactions to each other created humor and made the activity feel playful rather than serious. I think one of the prompts was act like you are a monster and scream as each person kind of leapt forward and scream/roared.

description: I'm at a crowded party with friends, and a man walks up to us with a deck of cards and asks if we want to see a magic trick. The trick involved a lot of participation, laughs, and surprises.
who_was_playing: Participant 1 (myself), Participant 2, Participant 3, Magician
trust_why: The environment was fun, so a spontaneous magic trick felt fitting for the experience
playful_why: The motion and misdirection of the performance made for a fun and stunning outcome
pull_why: My friends I have seen magic tricks online before but never in-person. This event sparked my curiosity as I thought in my head: can this person truly fool me?
signs_why: Lots of smiles and mouths open in shock. Exaggerated body movements from shock. Yells and gasps. I had many other friends to experience the trick after I had already done it.
feeling_why: Joy for the participants because it was a shocking magic trick. Joy for the magician that the trick worked.

description: My roommates and I found pieces of a couch on the curb, and convinced two other Northeastern Students passing by to help us carry it back to our apartment.
who_was_playing: Me, Roommate #1, Rommate #2, Stranger #1, Stranger #2
trust_why: This experience only occurred because the five of us immediately clicked with each other
playful_why: I would say it was playful in all ways except for sound. Motion is the most obvious, because the task required moving the couch from one place to another. However, shape was arguableyjust as important, because each couch piece was shaped differently, and some connected to others. This turned it into a puzzle, not only finding out how to connect the pieces to each other, but how to sling them around or on top of our bodies to get the best grip and balance. The color and texture also contributed, because the only reason the couch intrigued us and the main reason it caused such a scene was because it was bright orange and fuzzy.
pull_why: The biggest factor that led to the strangers joining was most likely just curiosity, with a hunt of physical challenge -- they were wandering out in the middle of the night and were approached with a random task of physical strength. They were talking to each other, comparing it to a "side quest" in a video game, where you take a deviation from your main objective for the sake of embarking on a quick, random experience with a possible reward.
signs_why: The puzzle-like aspect of finding the best ways to distribute and carry the pieces on our body contributed substantially to its playfulness.
feeling_why: I think the main draw for the two strangers was leaning into the silliness of joining our commotion, lugging around large bright objects on a busy street.

description: The project teams in my club were competing against each other. The goal was to throw a ping-pong ball into the other team’s cup. There were four rounds, and the team that won the most rounds advanced to the next stage.
who_was_playing: Every member of a project team
trust_why: We knew all the people playing is we are all in same club focusing on giving back to the community.
playful_why: Throwing the ball and seeing if it land in the cup was the playful part.
pull_why: When the pingpong ball landed in cup, it was a satisfying feeling as everyone cheer for you.
signs_why: The cheer and yelling people did after a ball was threw.
feeling_why: Trowing the ball and having people cheer for you was delightful.

description: I held a stuffed toy while my dog grabbed and pulled it with its mouth. We played tug-of-war together.
who_was_playing:
Player 1: Me, the human participant.
Player 2: My pet dog.
trust_why: The dog was familiar with me and trusted me, which made the play feel safe and comfortable
playful_why: The back-and-forth pulling and movement of the toy made the activity playful and engaging
pull_why: The dog immediately enjoyed pulling the toy and interacting with me, which encouraged it to keep playing

description: My sorority hosted a recruitment event where everyone made their own slime.
who_was_playing: Player 1) entire sorority; Player 2) potential new members
trust_why: The sorority girls and potential new members all created a fun, safe environment that encouraged everyone to make slime together.
playful_why: The texture of mixing the glue, borax, and shaving cream made this a fun activity.
pull_why: Combining all the ingredients to create a slime gave instant gratification.
signs_why: Everyone playing with their slime aggressively and moving it in different ways indicated the playfulness of the activity.
feeling_why: Making and playing with the slime brought instant joy to all of the girls.

description: I walked out to the kitchen to hear them laughing, and I immediately saw that they made a triple decker ricecake sandwich with peanut butter and greek yogurt inside. I was in shock with what I saw, and they were laughing about how tilted it was.  They said that they originally wanted to make a snack, and that all they had were those 3 ingredients. One of the roommates tried cracking the ricecake into two even slices, but accidentally made perfect thirds. That made them laugh, and eventually decided to roll with the new creation: the triple layer ricecake.
who_was_playing: 2 of my roommates, one loves to cook while the other prefers to freeze and air fry everything
trust_why: They were in our home kitchen with no one from the outside to judge the snack's outcome. They had the freedom to laugh at their creation rather than worry about a stranger's opinion.
playful_why: The crumbly texture of the rice cake made it hard to split cleanly in half. As a result, my roommate created three separate pieces, which was crucial in the final outcome. That sort of unpredictability is what turned a normal snack into an experiment.
pull_why: Instead of trying again, they wanted to see what they can make with what they had. They also had no expectation since they came across the discovery of only having the 3 ingredients at the time of making it.
signs_why: The yell was loud enough that I could hear it from my room. Lucky enough, I was already heading to the kitchen and got to see exactly what they were laughing at without having to actually ask them. That part made the experience more naturally playful because we all had no idea what to expect.
feeling_why: This observation showed me that play can come from a mistake. My roommates turned an initially failed trial of their vision into a funny and memorable recipe that we will definitely replicate in the future. Compared to my first observation, there were no rules or game at all. The play came entirely from an impulsive moment.
anything_else: When eating it, they also had so much trouble preventing a spill since they put too much yogurt inside. It was an effect from their initial thought to add more yogurt than they wanted because they wanted to see how much they could add. It made for a very funny moment.

activity: Playing "Cambia" on the top of the mountain
description: My friends and I went hiking on Saturday at Mt. Pemigewasset. We were very tired going all the way up and had barely any energy to make it to the summit. However, we finally made it and instead of just taking a few pictures and leaving, our friend realized he had brought cards (meant for later in the evening). We decided to impulsively sit down at the edge and play "Cambia" for 20 minutes.
who_was_playing: Me and my 4 closest friends from college. Since I had a tough schedule over the years, I did not have much time to hang out with them. They started playing this card game over summer when I was away, and when I came back they wanted to teach me it. Once we got to the top, we decided that I was going to learn how to play. The game started off as a learning lesson that quickly became an exciting competition between us, and the experience was one that I won't ever forget.
trust_why: The space was a odd place to play a card game. It was a cliffside where movements must be calculated. However, some of the space had a nice flat area where sitting down was safe. Once we found a good place to sit down, we quickly grew to trust the space and began playing the game.
playful_why: The orientation of the cards was important for this game, as we only had 4 cards each and had to remember the number of each card without looking. The game required pattern recognition and retention skills which created the competitiveness later in the game.
pull_why: For me, I wanted to see if I could learn how to play properly as quickly as possible. For my friends, the challenge was trying to teach me within a proper period of time to play and leave before the sun started to set. The ultimate challenge was finding a proper place to sit and not move around too much, which quickly became a sort of play.
signs: Behavior (linger, come back, repeat, invite a friend)
signs_why: The action of picking up your card only once to see the numbers challenged our retention and recall, which made the game fun. The behavior of observing what other cards my friends would put down and shaping a pattern in my head was repeated and almost perfected by the end of the game. The repetitions also gave a sense of excitement and shock to expect when someone would call "Cambia" in the end. The face expressions of pure joy for the winner (not me unfortunately) was felt across all players, which allowed us all to be happy regardless of the outcome.
feeling_why: Focus AND presence were the vibes of the game, as well as the environment we were in. We had to have a level of focus in the game to understand what cards my friends might have, as well as the cards I had. The element of presence was having some awarenees of our volume or occupied space as we were still in public and did not want to disturb the peace.
anything_else: All of the leading events allowed that specific game to be played. The fact that we were on a time constraint and that my friend randomly remembered his cards The fact that I never played before. The fact that we decided to make time to drive to this specific trail and walk all the way up. When I put it all together, it makes me realize how immersed we were in the moment and how small decisions and eventually lead up to a beautiful moment in time.

description: In between panels, a Black gospel choir came on stage and orchaestrated a 20-minute dance break
who_was_playing:
Gospel choir - leading the music
Audience - singing, dancing, chanting along
trust_why: Being in community with fellow Black folks (particularly Black christians) gave the space the energy of a Black church
playful_why: The gospel music was catchy, full of energy, and easy to sing/dance along to, which encouraged people to get out of their seats and join in
pull_why: Swept up by the energy of everyone else, the activity got more gratifying the more people participated
signs_why: Dancing, moving, smiling, laughing
feeling_why: The joy of being, singing, and dancing together
anything_else: I am not religious, and felt mildly uncomfortable by the random display of christian hegemony. But from a cultural standpoint, its very endearing to connect with others and let loose in this way, especially as a break from the polish and professionalism of the conference.

description: Played with our rain stick installation in snell.
who_was_playing: There was one person involved, who was flipping the object around.
trust_why: There were multiple set up in the space, which I think made it feel safer to interact with.
playful_why: The sound of the rice inside the rain stick is the most playful aspect, but the color and shape are also playful
pull_why: While some people interacted with it for visibility, to make their preferences seen to others, I think this individual was playing with it out of curiosity to see what would happen if they turned it.
signs: Behavior (linger, come back, repeat, invite a friend)
signs_why: The individual repeatedly turned it multiple times
feeling_why: The sound of the rain stick was a surprise, which I think instilled some sort of awe or curious feeling.

description: I was challenged to test my vertical
who_was_playing: Myself, people that went before and after me
trust_why: I saw other people doing the activity while I was walking, and the people organizing the activity seemed friendly
playful_why: I had three tries to jump as high as I could. It sparked curiosity and enjoyment for me.
pull_why: In my head I was thinking: could I get the highest vert on the leaderboard? (I got 3rd)
signs_why: I was smiling throughout the activity, as well as those who ran it and were watching. There was definitely a lot of excitement within the setting.
feeling_why: Focus to get the best vert

description: Had a long Monday, and had roughly 30 minutes to relax at home. I decided to watch a TV show, but  randomly stumbled upon the game Flappy Bird on the homepage. What started as a short play time ended up becoming an hour of forgetting the present. It made my day and allowed me to stay motivated with the rest of my tasks.
who_was_playing: Just me. My roommates were gone and I did not think there was any additional time to waste that day.
trust_why: lthough I did not have as much time to work with, I felt that the amount of time I initially gave myself, 30 minutes, was a safe amount that allowed me to forget about life for a little bit. It was as if the scarcity of time was what made the essence of play in this instance come to life.
playful_why: The button on the remote was a very smooth circle surrounded by a protruding circle that serves as the "D-pad". The smooth circle in the center is quite satisfying to press, and given that Flappy Bird is a one-button control game, it allowed for a smooth play experience. If the button had been too hard to press, it could have made me rage and ruined my relaxation time.
pull_why: I felt more inclined to say curiosity here because I genuinely did not realize that this concept was possible on the TV. The curiosity is what persuaded me to extend my playtime instead of going back to work, essentially invigorating those feelings of pure excitement. Urgency would have been a valid answer if I had known beforehand that Flappy Bird existed on the TV and that I could only play for 30 minutes.
signs_why: I found it extremely hard to play laying back on the couch, and performed better when I sat up and moved closer to the TV. My body posture allowed me to direct my attention towards the TV, and give my senses the best chance of reacting in time to surpass each obstacle in the game.
feeling_why: Instead of picking Awe or Wonder, which would align with curiosity slightly more, I believe that Joy and Delight came from the nostalgia I felt while playing. I felt 10 years old again and it was awesome, more so than I was in awe of how this game was available on the TV.
anything_else: Sometimes the feeling of playing is known right away or in the moment, and this moment was one of those. I usually do not realize I am playing until after the fact, but I learned almost immediately that this moment was perfect to document because I felt a sense of joy and delight in a time of stress and frustration. I learned to forget about life by giving in to strange stimulus (like a TV game?), and remembered how to play.

description: Weekly group stand-up meeting for a club. This club has a semester bingo competition between teams about team bonding. During this meeting, we decided to complete one of the bingo activities, "Try a team member's hobby". One of my teammates brought a deck of cards and tokens, so he taught us how to play poker, and then we spent the rest of the meeting playing poker.
who_was_playing: There were about 6 players involved in this game, a mix of second to fourth years, all members of Northeastern's Code4Community club. Player 1 taught the rest of the players how to play the game, as only half of the group had prior knowledge of how to play poker.
trust_why: I think that the fact that this play occured during a time already set aside for a club meeting meant people felt more inclined to participate in the play/activity then they would if it had been proposed for a different time. Something I noticed is that play that students would do is easiest to participate in if it is built into their schedule in some way, due to how busy all of Northeastern's students are.
playful_why: While the cards are colorful and feature fun shapes, I think the motion of drawing cards, hiding your hand, and the general movement of the cards was what lended the most playful aspect to the game.
pull_why: While the timing was what made the play possible, the ultimate motivation was competition, on two different levels. The first level is of course the competition within the game of Poker, while the second has to do with the Team Bonding Bingo Game/Competitiion which pushed us to play in the first place. Without the challenge, we likely wouldn't have played at alll.
signs_why: As a result of the play activity being a game of Poker, observing the other players mostly just showed them trying to remain blank-faced and concentrated on the game. However, while player's expressions were intentionally neutral; in spite of that, I noted a lot of conversation and laughter amogst everybody in the group relating to the poker game.
feeling_why: I think the larger group activity, learning and practice a new game, made for a very joyful experience, on ethat shows the happiness (and other emotions of the brain). We were delighted to learn a new game, and to play it together.
